import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.58

by A. N. Skiba

Is the subsemigroup generated by the undecomposable formations in the
semigroup of formations of finite groups free?

A *formation* is a nonempty class of finite groups that is closed under
homomorphic images and under finite subdirect products (if $N_1, N_2 \trianglelefteq G$
with $G/N_1, G/N_2 \in \mathfrak{F}$, then $G/(N_1 \cap N_2) \in \mathfrak{F}$).
For a formation $\mathfrak{G}$ and a finite group $G$, the
$\mathfrak{G}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{G}}$ is the smallest normal subgroup $N$ of $G$
with $G/N \in \mathfrak{G}$. The (Gaschütz) product of two formations is
$\mathfrak{F}\mathfrak{G} = \{G : G^{\mathfrak{G}} \in \mathfrak{F}\}$. By a theorem of
Gaschütz the product of two formations is again a formation, and the product is
associative, so the formations of finite groups form a semigroup, whose identity
is the formation $(1)$ of trivial groups. A formation $\mathfrak{F} \neq (1)$ is
*undecomposable* if $\mathfrak{F} = \mathfrak{M}\mathfrak{H}$ for formations
$\mathfrak{M}, \mathfrak{H}$ forces $\mathfrak{M} = (1)$ or $\mathfrak{H} = (1)$.

The empty class is excluded from the formations considered here. It is neither
undecomposable nor a product of undecomposable formations (with the usual convention
that it is a zero of the semigroup), so this does not affect the question.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- K. Doerk, T. Hawkes, *Finite Soluble Groups*, de Gruyter, 1992, Chapter IV, Section 1.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.58»

/-- A class of finite groups, given by a predicate on finite groups (with carrier in
`Type`, which is no restriction up to isomorphism). Equality of two classes is equality
of these predicates. -/
@[ext]
structure FiniteGroupClass where
  /-- Membership of a finite group `G` in the class. -/
  mem : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], Prop

namespace FiniteGroupClass

/-- The class $(1)$ of trivial groups. It is the identity of the semigroup of
formations. -/
instance : One FiniteGroupClass where
  one := ⟨fun G _ _ => Subsingleton G⟩

/-- The class $\mathfrak{E}$ of all finite groups. -/
def univ : FiniteGroupClass := ⟨fun _ _ _ => True⟩

/-- A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups is a formation if it is nonempty, closed under
homomorphic images (this includes closure under isomorphism), and closed under finite
subdirect products: if $N_1, N_2 \trianglelefteq G$ with $G/N_1, G/N_2 \in \mathfrak{F}$,
then $G/(N_1 \cap N_2) \in \mathfrak{F}$. -/
structure IsFormation (𝔉 : FiniteGroupClass) : Prop where
  /-- The class is nonempty. -/
  nonempty : ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G), 𝔉.mem G
  /-- The class is closed under homomorphic images. -/
  mem_of_surjective : ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] [Group H] [Finite H] (f : G →* H),
    Function.Surjective f → 𝔉.mem G → 𝔉.mem H
  /-- The class is closed under finite subdirect products. -/
  mem_quotient_inf : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (N₁ N₂ : Subgroup G)
    [N₁.Normal] [N₂.Normal], 𝔉.mem (G ⧸ N₁) → 𝔉.mem (G ⧸ N₂) → 𝔉.mem (G ⧸ (N₁ ⊓ N₂))

/-- The $\mathfrak{G}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{G}}$ of a finite group $G$: the intersection
of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{G}$. When $\mathfrak{G}$ is a
formation, this is the smallest normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{G}$. -/
def residual (𝔊 : FiniteGroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : Subgroup G :=
  ⨅ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal) (_ : 𝔊.mem (G ⧸ N)), N

instance (𝔊 : FiniteGroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : (𝔊.residual G).Normal :=
  Subgroup.normal_iInf_normal fun _ => Subgroup.normal_iInf_normal fun hN =>
    Subgroup.normal_iInf_normal fun _ => hN

/-- The Gaschütz product $\mathfrak{F}\mathfrak{G} = \{G : G^{\mathfrak{G}} \in \mathfrak{F}\}$
of two classes of finite groups. -/
instance : Mul FiniteGroupClass where
  mul 𝔉 𝔊 := ⟨fun G _ _ => 𝔉.mem (𝔊.residual G)⟩

/-- A formation $\mathfrak{F} \neq (1)$ is undecomposable if it is not the product of two
formations both different from $(1)$. -/
def IsUndecomposable (𝔉 : FiniteGroupClass) : Prop :=
  IsFormation 𝔉 ∧ 𝔉 ≠ 1 ∧
    ∀ 𝔐 ℌ : FiniteGroupClass, IsFormation 𝔐 → IsFormation ℌ → 𝔐 ≠ 1 → ℌ ≠ 1 → 𝔉 ≠ 𝔐 * ℌ

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem mul_mem_iff (𝔉 𝔊 : FiniteGroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    (𝔉 * 𝔊).mem G ↔ 𝔉.mem (𝔊.residual G) :=
  Iff.rfl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFormation_univ : IsFormation univ where
  nonempty := ⟨Unit, inferInstance, inferInstance, trivial⟩
  mem_of_surjective := by intros; trivial
  mem_quotient_inf := by intros; trivial

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFormation_one : IsFormation 1 where
  nonempty := ⟨Unit, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton Unit)⟩
  mem_of_surjective := by
    intro G H _ _ _ _ f hf h
    exact @Function.Surjective.subsingleton _ _ _ h hf
  mem_quotient_inf := by
    intro G _ _ N₁ N₂ _ _ h₁ h₂
    refine QuotientGroup.subsingleton_iff.mpr ?_
    rw [QuotientGroup.subsingleton_iff.mp h₁, QuotientGroup.subsingleton_iff.mp h₂, inf_idem]

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem residual_one (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : (1 : FiniteGroupClass).residual G = ⊤ :=
  le_antisymm le_top <| le_iInf fun _ => le_iInf fun _ => le_iInf fun h =>
    (QuotientGroup.subsingleton_iff.mp h).ge

end FiniteGroupClass

open FiniteGroupClass

/--
Is the subsemigroup generated by the undecomposable formations in the semigroup of
formations of finite groups free?

The subsemigroup generated by the undecomposable formations consists of the products
$\mathfrak{F}_1 \cdots \mathfrak{F}_n$ ($n \geq 1$) of undecomposable formations. It is
free on the undecomposable formations exactly when every such product has a unique
factorization: if $\mathfrak{F}_1 \cdots \mathfrak{F}_n = \mathfrak{G}_1 \cdots \mathfrak{G}_m$
with all $\mathfrak{F}_i, \mathfrak{G}_j$ undecomposable, then $n = m$ and
$\mathfrak{F}_i = \mathfrak{G}_i$ for all $i$. Since the undecomposable formations are
exactly the elements of this subsemigroup that are not products of two of its elements,
this is also equivalent to the subsemigroup being abstractly a free semigroup.

Products of lists are taken with `List.prod`, which right-associates; by Gaschütz's theorem
the product of formations is associative, so the bracketing is immaterial.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.58» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ l₁ l₂ : List FiniteGroupClass, l₁ ≠ [] → l₂ ≠ [] →
      (∀ 𝔉 ∈ l₁, IsUndecomposable 𝔉) → (∀ 𝔉 ∈ l₂, IsUndecomposable 𝔉) →
      l₁.prod = l₂.prod → l₁ = l₂ := by

end Kourovka.«10.58»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.58

by A. N. Skiba

Is the subsemigroup generated by the undecomposable formations in the semigroup of
formations of finite groups free?

A *formation* is a nonempty class of finite groups (closed under isomorphism) that is closed
under taking quotients and under finite subdirect products (if $G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ lie in the
class then so does $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$). The empty class is not counted as a formation, so that
residuals are always defined. For a formation $\mathfrak{H}$ and a finite group $G$, the
$\mathfrak{H}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{H}}$ is the smallest normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with
$G/N \in \mathfrak{H}$. The (Gaschütz) product of two formations is
$\mathfrak{F}\mathfrak{H} = \{G : G^{\mathfrak{H}} \in \mathfrak{F}\}$; it is again a
formation, the product is associative, and the formation $(1)$ of trivial groups is the
identity. This is the semigroup of formations of finite groups.

A formation $\mathfrak{F} \neq (1)$ is *undecomposable* if it cannot be written as a product
$\mathfrak{F} = \mathfrak{M}\mathfrak{H}$ of two formations $\mathfrak{M}, \mathfrak{H} \neq (1)$.
The problem asks whether the subsemigroup generated by the undecomposable formations is free,
i.e. freely generated by the undecomposable formations: every product of undecomposable
formations has a unique factorization into undecomposable formations.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.58»

/-- A class of finite groups, given by a membership predicate on finite groups. -/
@[ext]
structure GroupClass where
  /-- The membership predicate of the class. -/
  Mem : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], Prop

/-- A *formation* of finite groups: a nonempty class of finite groups that is closed under
isomorphism, under taking quotients, and under finite subdirect products, i.e. if
$G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ lie in the class then so does $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$. -/
structure Formation extends GroupClass where
  /-- A formation is nonempty. -/
  nonempty : ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G), Mem G
  /-- A formation is closed under isomorphism. -/
  mem_of_mulEquiv : ∀ {G H : Type} [Group G] [Finite G] [Group H] [Finite H],
    G ≃* H → Mem G → Mem H
  /-- A formation is closed under taking quotients. -/
  mem_quotient : ∀ {G : Type} [Group G] [Finite G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal],
    Mem G → Mem (G ⧸ N)
  /-- A formation is closed under finite subdirect products. -/
  mem_quotient_inf : ∀ {G : Type} [Group G] [Finite G] (N₁ N₂ : Subgroup G)
    [N₁.Normal] [N₂.Normal], Mem (G ⧸ N₁) → Mem (G ⧸ N₂) → Mem (G ⧸ (N₁ ⊓ N₂))

namespace GroupClass

/-- The $\mathfrak{F}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{F}}$ of a finite group $G$ with respect to a class
$\mathfrak{F}$: the intersection of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{F}$.
For a formation $\mathfrak{F}$ this is the smallest such normal subgroup. -/
def residual (𝔉 : GroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : Subgroup G :=
  sInf {N : Subgroup G | ∃ _ : N.Normal, 𝔉.Mem (G ⧸ N)}

/-- The class $(1)$ of trivial groups. It is the identity of the semigroup of formations. -/
instance : One GroupClass := ⟨⟨fun G _ _ => Subsingleton G⟩⟩

/-- The (Gaschütz) product $\mathfrak{F}\mathfrak{H} = \{G : G^{\mathfrak{H}} \in \mathfrak{F}\}$
of two classes of finite groups. The product of two formations is again a formation. -/
instance : Mul GroupClass := ⟨fun 𝔉 ℌ => ⟨fun G _ _ => 𝔉.Mem (ℌ.residual G)⟩⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem one_mem_iff (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : (1 : GroupClass).Mem G ↔ Subsingleton G :=
  Iff.rfl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mul_mem_iff (𝔉 ℌ : GroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    (𝔉 * ℌ).Mem G ↔ 𝔉.Mem (ℌ.residual G) :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The $(1)$-residual of a finite group $G$ is $G$ itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem residual_one (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : (1 : GroupClass).residual G = ⊤ := by
  have h : {N : Subgroup G | ∃ _ : N.Normal, (1 : GroupClass).Mem (G ⧸ N)} = {⊤} := by
    ext N
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff, one_mem_iff, QuotientGroup.subsingleton_iff]
    exact ⟨fun ⟨_, hN⟩ => hN, fun hN => ⟨hN ▸ inferInstance, hN⟩⟩
  rw [residual, h, sInf_singleton]

end GroupClass

namespace Formation

/-- The trivial formation $(1)$, consisting of the trivial groups. -/
def one : Formation where
  toGroupClass := 1
  nonempty := ⟨Unit, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
  mem_of_mulEquiv := by
    intro G H _ _ _ _ e h
    rw [GroupClass.one_mem_iff] at h ⊢
    exact e.symm.toEquiv.subsingleton
  mem_quotient := by
    intro G _ _ N _ h
    rw [GroupClass.one_mem_iff] at h ⊢
    exact Quotient.instSubsingletonQuotient _
  mem_quotient_inf := by
    intro G _ _ N₁ N₂ _ _ h₁ h₂
    rw [GroupClass.one_mem_iff, QuotientGroup.subsingleton_iff] at h₁ h₂ ⊢
    rw [h₁, h₂, inf_idem]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem one_toGroupClass : one.toGroupClass = 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The trivial formation is a right identity for the product. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem toGroupClass_mul_one (𝔉 : Formation) : 𝔉.toGroupClass * 1 = 𝔉.toGroupClass := by
  ext G _ _
  rw [GroupClass.mul_mem_iff, GroupClass.residual_one]
  exact ⟨𝔉.mem_of_mulEquiv Subgroup.topEquiv, 𝔉.mem_of_mulEquiv Subgroup.topEquiv.symm⟩

/-- A formation $\mathfrak{F}$ is *undecomposable* if $\mathfrak{F} \neq (1)$ and $\mathfrak{F}$
cannot be written as a product $\mathfrak{M}\mathfrak{H}$ of two formations
$\mathfrak{M}, \mathfrak{H} \neq (1)$. -/
def IsUndecomposable (𝔉 : Formation) : Prop :=
  𝔉.toGroupClass ≠ 1 ∧ ¬ ∃ 𝔐 ℌ : Formation, 𝔐.toGroupClass ≠ 1 ∧ ℌ.toGroupClass ≠ 1 ∧
    𝔉.toGroupClass = 𝔐.toGroupClass * ℌ.toGroupClass

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isUndecomposable_one : ¬ one.IsUndecomposable :=
  fun h => h.1 rfl

end Formation

/--
Is the subsemigroup generated by the undecomposable formations in the semigroup of
formations of finite groups free?

Freeness is understood as: the subsemigroup is freely generated by the undecomposable
formations, i.e. if $\mathfrak{F}_1 \cdots \mathfrak{F}_n = \mathfrak{H}_1 \cdots \mathfrak{H}_m$
with all $\mathfrak{F}_i$, $\mathfrak{H}_j$ undecomposable formations and $n, m \geq 1$, then
$n = m$ and $\mathfrak{F}_i = \mathfrak{H}_i$ for all $i$. Products of formations are computed
as classes of finite groups, using the Gaschütz product on classes; the product of formations
is again a formation, so this agrees with the product in the semigroup of formations.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.58» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ l₁ l₂ : List Formation, l₁ ≠ [] → l₂ ≠ [] →
      (∀ 𝔉 ∈ l₁, 𝔉.IsUndecomposable) → (∀ 𝔉 ∈ l₂, 𝔉.IsUndecomposable) →
      (l₁.map Formation.toGroupClass).prod = (l₂.map Formation.toGroupClass).prod →
      l₁ = l₂ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.58»

A *formation* of finite groups is a nonempty class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups
(closed under isomorphism) such that
* if $G \in \mathfrak{F}$ and $N \trianglelefteq G$ then $G/N \in \mathfrak{F}$, and
* if $N_1, N_2 \trianglelefteq G$ with $G/N_1, G/N_2 \in \mathfrak{F}$ then
  $G/(N_1 \cap N_2) \in \mathfrak{F}$.

For a finite group $G$, the $\mathfrak{F}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{F}}$ is the intersection of all
normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{F}$. The (Gaschütz) product of two formations
is $\mathfrak{F}\mathfrak{H} = \{G : G^{\mathfrak{H}} \in \mathfrak{F}\}$. This product of two
formations is again a formation and it is associative, so the formations of finite groups form a
semigroup; its identity is the formation $(1)$ of trivial groups. A formation is *nontrivial* if
it is different from $(1)$, and it is *undecomposable* if it is nontrivial and is not the product
of two nontrivial formations.

The subsemigroup generated by the undecomposable formations is free (on the set of undecomposable
formations) exactly when every element of it has a unique representation as a product of
undecomposable formations, i.e. when the natural map from the free semigroup on the set of
undecomposable formations is injective.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.58»

/--
A class of finite groups, given by a predicate on finite groups.

Groups are taken in `Type`; this loses nothing since every finite group is isomorphic to a group
in `Type`.
-/
@[ext]
structure GroupClass where
  /-- Membership of the finite group `G` in the class. -/
  Mem (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : Prop

namespace GroupClass

/--
The `𝔉`-residual $G^{\mathfrak{F}}$ of a finite group `G`: the intersection of all normal
subgroups `N` of `G` with `G ⧸ N ∈ 𝔉`.
-/
def residual (𝔉 : GroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : Subgroup G :=
  ⨅ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal) (_ : 𝔉.Mem (G ⧸ N)), N

/--
The (Gaschütz) product of two classes of finite groups:
$\mathfrak{F}\mathfrak{H} = \{G : G^{\mathfrak{H}} \in \mathfrak{F}\}$.
-/
instance : Mul GroupClass where
  mul 𝔉 ℌ := ⟨fun G _ _ => 𝔉.Mem (ℌ.residual G)⟩

/-- The class $(1)$ of trivial groups. -/
instance : One GroupClass where
  one := ⟨fun G _ _ => Subsingleton G⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_mul_iff (𝔉 ℌ : GroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    (𝔉 * ℌ).Mem G ↔ 𝔉.Mem (ℌ.residual G) :=
  Iff.rfl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_one_iff (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    (1 : GroupClass).Mem G ↔ Subsingleton G :=
  Iff.rfl

/--
A formation of finite groups: a nonempty class of finite groups that is closed under
isomorphism, under quotients, and under finite subdirect products (if `G ⧸ N₁` and `G ⧸ N₂` lie
in the class, so does `G ⧸ (N₁ ⊓ N₂)`).
-/
structure IsFormation (𝔉 : GroupClass) : Prop where
  nonempty : ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G), 𝔉.Mem G
  mem_of_mulEquiv : ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] [Group H] [Finite H],
    (G ≃* H) → 𝔉.Mem G → 𝔉.Mem H
  mem_quotient : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal],
    𝔉.Mem G → 𝔉.Mem (G ⧸ N)
  mem_quotient_inf : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (N₁ N₂ : Subgroup G)
    [N₁.Normal] [N₂.Normal], 𝔉.Mem (G ⧸ N₁) → 𝔉.Mem (G ⧸ N₂) → 𝔉.Mem (G ⧸ (N₁ ⊓ N₂))

/--
A formation `𝔉` of finite groups is *undecomposable* if it is nontrivial, i.e. `𝔉 ≠ (1)`,
and it is not the product `𝔊 * ℌ` of two nontrivial formations `𝔊`, `ℌ`.
-/
def IsUndecomposableFormation (𝔉 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  𝔉.IsFormation ∧ 𝔉 ≠ 1 ∧
    ¬ ∃ 𝔊 ℌ : GroupClass, 𝔊.IsFormation ∧ ℌ.IsFormation ∧ 𝔊 ≠ 1 ∧ ℌ ≠ 1 ∧ 𝔉 = 𝔊 * ℌ

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem residual_one (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] : (1 : GroupClass).residual G = ⊤ := by
  refine top_le_iff.mp (le_iInf₂ fun N _ ↦ le_iInf fun h ↦ ?_)
  rw [mem_one_iff, QuotientGroup.subsingleton_iff] at h
  exact h.ge

/-- The class `1` is a right identity for the product on isomorphism-closed classes. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mul_one_of_mem_of_mulEquiv (𝔉 : GroupClass)
    (h : ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] [Group H] [Finite H], (G ≃* H) → 𝔉.Mem G → 𝔉.Mem H) :
    𝔉 * 1 = 𝔉 := by
  ext G _ _
  rw [mem_mul_iff, residual_one]
  exact ⟨h _ _ Subgroup.topEquiv, h _ _ Subgroup.topEquiv.symm⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFormation_one : (1 : GroupClass).IsFormation := by
  refine ⟨⟨Unit, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro G H _ _ _ _ e h
    rw [mem_one_iff] at h ⊢
    exact e.symm.injective.subsingleton
  · intro G _ _ N _ h
    rw [mem_one_iff] at h ⊢
    exact Quotient.instSubsingletonQuotient _
  · intro G _ _ N₁ N₂ _ _ h₁ h₂
    rw [mem_one_iff, QuotientGroup.subsingleton_iff] at h₁ h₂ ⊢
    rw [h₁, h₂, inf_idem]

end GroupClass

modeling_decisions: The 'semigroup of formations' is taken to consist of nonempty formations (the empty class breaks associativity of the Gaschütz product); nonemptiness is a field of `IsFormation`. This matches the table's note that the identity is the formation of trivial groups.

The Gaschütz product and identity are defined on arbitrary classes of finite groups (`GroupClass`) rather than on a bundled type of formations; the facts that the product of two formations is a formation and that it is associative are stated in the docstring but not proved, since they are not needed to state the question (the theorem quantifies over lists whose entries are formations and compares the resulting classes).

'Free' is read as freely generated by the set of undecomposable formations: for nonempty lists l₁, l₂ of undecomposable formations, `l₁.prod = l₂.prod → l₁ = l₂`. This is the injectivity of the canonical map from the free semigroup on the undecomposables; it also coincides with the 'abstractly free' reading, since the basis of a free semigroup is its set of indecomposable elements and these are exactly the undecomposable formations here.

`List.prod` is right-nested and ends with a factor `1`; the API lemma `mul_one_of_mem_of_mulEquiv` proves `𝔉 * 1 = 𝔉` for isomorphism-closed classes, so `l.prod` is exactly the iterated Gaschütz product of the formations in `l`. The order convention 𝔉𝔊 = {G : G^𝔊 ∈ 𝔉} follows Skiba/Shemetkov; freeness is in any case invariant under reversing the product.

Groups are taken in `Type` (universe 0); every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, so nothing is lost. The trivial class is `Subsingleton G`. Closure under finite subdirect products is stated in its binary form (G/N₁, G/N₂ ∈ 𝔉 ⇒ G/(N₁ ⊓ N₂) ∈ 𝔉), the standard textbook definition equivalent to R₀-closure for finite groups together with isomorphism closure.
